problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}4x-2y+3z=0 \\ 8x-3y+5z=1 \\ 7x-2y+4z=1\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, what is the value of $x+y+z?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*

$$
\,{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & -5 & 4 \\ 5 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

feedback.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+2y+z=0 \\ x+3y+z=-1 \\ 2x-3y-z=-2\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, what is the value of $\frac{yz}{x}?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*

$$
\,{A}^{-1}=-\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & -1 \\ 3 & -3 & 0 \\ -9 & 7 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's write our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & -3 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & -1 \\ 3 & -3 & 0 \\ -9 & 7 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution is $x=-1,y=-1,z=3.$

Finally, $\frac{yz}{x}=\frac{(-1)\cdot 3}{-1}=3.$
